one_line_contribution: Reframes retrieved-experience memory harm as a procedural failure — the agent stops gathering evidence early because memory hands it an outcome — and tests that reframing with a token-matched outcome-redaction contrast, a content-free evidence floor applied to both memory and memory-free arms as an interaction, and a claim that a GEPA-searched instruction cannot substitute for the floor.
closest_prior_work: The proposal correctly identifies Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following / misaligned experience replay) and concedes the phenomenon to it; that concession is fair and handled honestly, and the mediation framing does survive it. The threats it misses are outside the agent-memory literature and are more damaging to the individual components. First, the 'evidence floor' is attribution-gated answering, which is a solved-and-published RAG design: citation-constrained generation (ALCE-style 'generate text with citations'), Self-RAG's retrieve/critique tokens, and FLARE/IRCoT's retrieve-until-supported control flow all already enforce 'do not answer until your own retrieval supports the answer', and all already report that it reduces unsupported answers. The paper would therefore be claiming a known intervention as its causal instrument; the novelty must live entirely in the memory-by-floor interaction, which the writing does not make clear. Second, and worse for the mediator, MuSiQue (Trivedi et al., 2022) — one of the three pooled datasets — was constructed around a disconnected-reasoning (DiRe) probe that measures exactly whether a system produced the answer without performing the intermediate hops, and Min et al. 2019 ('Compositional questions do not necessitate multi-hop reasoning') established that HotpotQA-distractor is largely answerable by single-hop shortcutting. 'Evidence sufficiency' is a rebadged DiRe, and 'agents in multi-hop QA answer without gathering the evidence' is the baseline state of these benchmarks, not a memory effect. Neither line is cited.
strongest_objection: The title claim — that instruction optimization cannot repair this — is over-determined by the design rather than tested by it, and the headline interaction is underpowered by the proposal's own arithmetic. (a) On claim (iii): G1's failure is guaranteed by three independent design choices. GEPA is selected on train-split task accuracy, not on floor compliance or trajectory length; on a 150-instance train split with a ~10% break rate there are roughly 15 informative broken episodes to reflect over; and 400 rollouts is a thin search. If memory is net-positive on the train split (the precheck only requires breaks ≥4% and fixes ≥4%), there is no selection pressure toward 'keep looking' at all, so 'G1 recovers <1/3 of the floor's benefit' is a prediction about this GEPA configuration's objective and budget, not about the instruction slot. Worse, the comparison is structurally a hard programmatic constraint versus a politely worded request, and the fact that models comply with enforced constraints more than with instructions is known a priori — it is not a discovery about what prompt optimization can own, and it certainly does not license 'some agent pathologies are not addressable by prompt optimization at all'. The proposal's own mitigation (report the evolved text, report the score trajectory) does not remove the objective mismatch. (b) On power: breaks under M1 are budgeted at ~50/500 = 10 points. Prediction 3 asks for ≥50% break reduction under M1+Fh (≥5 points) with M0+Fh gaining less than a third of that (<1.7 points), so the predicted interaction is ~3.3 points — against a stated interaction MDE of ~6 points. The headline causal test is, by the proposal's own numbers, powered at roughly half the effect it predicts, and this is before the Holm correction across a family of eleven-plus arms, which the α=0.05 MDE calculation does not absorb. If the precheck merely clears its 4% gate, a halving of breaks is a 2-point effect against a 6-point MDE and the central experiment cannot return a result in either direction. (c) A secondary but real problem: the floor is defined as 'the agent may not answer until it has itself retrieved supporting spans', and the mediator is defined as 'do the supporting spans appear in this episode's own retrievals'. The causal instrument is the operational negation of the mediator, so Analysis 2 is close to definitionally true and carries less evidential weight than its billing as 'the causal test' suggests. Similarly, with an ExpeL bank built from the training splits of the same three datasets, a retrieved item for a near-duplicate question will often contain a directly appropriable answer string; predicting memory-echo >40% on wrong answers concedes that the phenomenon may reduce to answer-copying, and M3 ('outcome-only shortcuts maximally') is then near-tautological rather than a mechanism finding.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Fix the power on the endpoint that carries the paper: enrich the test set for break-eligible instances using the dev bank and precheck (stratified sampling of instances where memory is retrieved with high similarity), or raise n on the M1/M1+Fh/M0/M0+Fh cells specifically and cut arms elsewhere, and re-derive the interaction MDE under the Holm-corrected alpha. State the interaction MDE conditional on the precheck's observed break rate, not on the optimistic 10% figure. (2) Make (iii) falsifiable in the direction that would refute it: give GEPA a rollout-budget scaling curve (e.g. 400 / 1600 / 6400) so a plateau is evidence rather than an artifact; run at least one second optimizer (MIPRO) so the claim is about instruction search rather than about GEPA; and give one variant an objective that includes evidence sufficiency or compliance, so a failure cannot be attributed to the optimizer never having been asked. Then retitle to what the design supports — something like 'instruction-level repairs underperform a control-flow floor at matched search budget' — rather than 'instruction optimization cannot repair it'. (3) Add the crossed cells the factorial omits: M2+Fh, M3+Fh and G1+Fh. Without G1+Fh the enforcement-versus-discovery story is asserted from the compliance readout alone; without M2+Fh you cannot tell whether redaction and the floor are addressing the same mechanism or are additive, which is the difference between a mechanism paper and two separate interventions. (4) Break the answer-copying confound: add an outcome-mismatched arm (same task family, procedure intact, outcome shuffled from a different instance so it is outcome-bearing but not appropriable). If truncation happens there too, the mechanism is 'an outcome terminates the search'; if it does not, the mechanism is 'memory supplied a usable answer' and the paper is a copying study. Also drop or heavily de-emphasize Analysis 5, whose fingerprint is guaranteed by construction since the bank is built pre-perturbation.
missing_baseline: Memory-dropout at the answer step: memory injected during planning and tool use, then removed from context before the final-answer turn. This is cheap, content-free, and lives in the control flow like the floor, but it discriminates exactly the hypothesis under test — if removing memory only at termination recovers most of M1+Fh's break reduction, the harm is that memory supplies an answer at commitment time, not that it truncates the search, and the entire premature-termination framing collapses into memory-echo. The plan has no arm that separates these. Two further omissions a reviewer will raise: (a) a runtime memory-gating / selective-injection baseline (inject only when a calibrated signal says the item will help, or inject k adaptively per instance) — this is the track's own open question and it lives in the demonstration slot, which the paper's instruction-versus-control-flow dichotomy silently excludes, so a cheap gate matching the floor would undercut the division-of-labour framing; and (b) the crossed cells G1+Fh, M2+Fh, M3+Fh, and M4+Fh.
preprint_collision: Above average for this kind of submission and clearly done rather than asserted: it names one specific closest work with an arXiv ID, concedes the phenomenon to it, states the manipulation that distinguishes the two, and gives a condition under which the prior work is complete and this proposal is wrong. That is the right shape. Three problems. First, credibility: the section itself discloses that an earlier draft cited a dozen forward-dated arXiv IDs the author could not verify. That history means the remaining IDs cannot be taken on trust, and every entry except 2505.16067 is a 2026 identifier (2604.27003, 2605.24941, 2607.06595, 2608.02508, 2605.18930) that a reviewer cannot confirm from the submission. The novelty case therefore rests on exactly one verifiable anchor while claiming a clean field around it. Second, the search is scoped entirely to agent-memory keywords and misses the two literatures that actually threaten the components: RAG attribution and adaptive-retrieval work (Self-RAG, FLARE, IRCoT, citation-gated answering) makes the evidence floor a published intervention rather than a new instrument, and multi-hop shortcut work (Min et al. 2019 on HotpotQA; MuSiQue's own disconnected-reasoning probe) makes 'evidence sufficiency' a rebadged existing metric and establishes the base-rate shortcutting the study attributes to memory. Neither is mentioned, so the check's 'explicit gap statement' is narrower than it reads. Third, the honest caveat is correct and load-bearing: no OpenReview sweep was performed, and by the proposal's own admission an outcome-redaction or step-floor ablation plausibly sits in a recent agent-memory appendix. I would not call this a collision, but I would not treat the novelty as established either — it is one verified citation plus a set of unverifiable ones, with the adjacent 2604.27003 conceded as a near-miss on the paper's own key content contrast.
